drug_class: Antiprotozoal / Antiparasitic (also used as an antifungal in certain cases)
purpose: Pentamidine is used to treat or prevent a serious lung infection called Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), which most often affects people with weakened immune systems, such as those living with HIV/AIDS. It can be given as an injection to treat an active infection or inhaled as a mist to help prevent the infection from occurring in the first place.
how_it_works: Pentamidine works by interfering with the DNA and essential functions of the tiny organisms that cause the infection, stopping them from growing and multiplying. Think of it as disrupting the germ's ability to survive and reproduce inside your body. Over time, this helps your immune system clear the infection.
common_side_effects: Inhaled form: cough, wheezing, shortness of breath, metallic taste in the mouth, and mild throat irritation. Injected form: low blood pressure, nausea, vomiting, low blood sugar, dizziness, decreased appetite, and pain or redness at the injection site.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious drops in blood sugar or blood pressure, especially with the injected form, so your blood sugar and blood pressure will be monitored closely. It can also affect your kidneys, liver, and heart rhythm, so regular lab tests are important. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or have kidney, liver, or heart problems. Inhaled pentamidine does not fully protect others around you from infection, so precautions may still be needed.
typical_dosing: Injected (treatment): Usually 4 mg per kilogram of your body weight given once daily through an IV or into a muscle for about 14 to 21 days, as directed by your doctor. Inhaled (prevention): Typically 300 mg inhaled through a special nebulizer device once every 4 weeks. Your doctor will determine the exact dose and schedule that is right for you.
